newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunker in Berlin probably belonged to Speer.
newsitem.headline: Bunker in Berlin probably belonged to Speer.

text.p: A World War two bunker containing furniture, cutlery and telephones which was discovered at a Berlin building site last December was probably used by Albert Speer, a spokesman at the site said on Thursday.
The 225 square metre (2,400 square foot) concrete bunker was unearthed by workers who are building a regional office for DG Bank.

"The bunker was most likely used by Albert Speer and his people, but we need to keep researching the bunker's history," said bank spokesman Christian Schilling. He said there was nothing which appeared to belong to Speer in the bunker.

Speer was a close aide of Adolf Hitler and served as his armaments minister and architect. He remained at Hitler's side until his escape shortly before the end of the war. He was later convicted of war crimes and sentenced to 20 years in prison, which he served in Berlin's notorious Spandau prison.
The bank will blow up the bunker next week in order to clear room for the building's foundation if permission from city authorities is granted, Schilling said.
